Perth, Full Time, Construction
Vacancy Listing Dates 14/07/2026 to 11/08/2026
Please Quote Reference Number 17581
- Seeking qualified applicants
- Full time opportunity
- Join the ECC United team working across Perth and WA

Company Overview:

Based in Perth, Western Australia, ECC United Pty Ltd are an established and growing construction company specialising in residential projects, with a strong expansion into the commercial construction sector. Our work includes:
- Construction: ECC United (elemental construction and consulting) is expanding its services to include the planning and delivery of multi-unit residential developments, comprising 20 to 30 dwellings with integrated roads, parking, landscaped open spaces, and community facilities. This expansion strengthens our capability to deliver larger, sustainable developments while maintaining our commitment to quality, environmental responsibility, and regulatory compliance.
- Consultation
- Site assessments
- Land management
- Regulatory compliance

We pride ourselves on operational excellence, quality, and strict regulatory compliance across all our sites.

About the position:

The Environmental & Project Compliance Officer will manage our in-house environmental compliance frameworks while providing necessary operational support to our project delivery teams. Key responsibilities including:
- Prepare, lodge, and manage Environmental Management Plans (EMPs) required for development approvals across Councils
- Prepare and review environmental compliance reports, Bushfire Attack Level (BAL) assessments where applicable, and other supporting documentation required for project approvals.
- Coordinate and interpret geotechnical assessments, site classifications, and Acid Sulphate Soil (ASS) management plans. Oversee erosion, sediment, and sand drift controls on active sites
- Develop, implement, and monitor Site Waste Minimisation Plans in accordance with Western Australian resource recovery and environmental policies.
- Conduct regular environmental and safety inspections across residential and commercial sites to ensure compliance with dust, noise, vibration, and chemical storage bylaws. Maintain accurate compliance logs for final council sign-offs
- Assess site conditions and provide recommendations for soil management, land rehabilitation, stormwater management, irrigation, and drainage solutions.
- Identify and implement sustainability initiatives to minimise environmental impacts and improve resource efficiency during construction.
- Review survey information, engineering drawings, and environmental documentation to support planning and construction activities.
- Liaise with clients, consultants, contractors, local authorities, and regulatory agencies on environmental matters.
- Assist with project documentation, including material take-offs, environmental compliance records, and variation documentation where environmental considerations are involved.
- Support Site Supervisors by monitoring environmental aspects of Work Health and Safety (WHS), maintaining environmental incident records, and contributing to environmental site inductions and awareness programs.

Required:
- Tertiary qualification in Environmental Science, Agricultural Science, Environmental Engineering, or a highly analytical/scientific discipline.
- Ideally at least one year of experience in the relevant field.
- Strong foundational knowledge in soil science, and environmental reporting.
- Exceptional report-writing and analytical skills, with the ability to interpret technical data and translate it into practical site solutions.
- Highly organised with the ability to multitask in a fast-paced construction environment.
- Current WA Driver’s License and a White Card (Construction Induction).

Location: HQ: Perth, WA, across different sites

Salary: $80,000 - $90,000 plus super

Apply now through our online application form -
https://www.netyourjob.com.au/jobs/17581.php

REDEEM SKILLS RECRUITMENT SOLUTIONS (RECRUITER) on behalf of CareSquad Pty Ltd T/A Care Squad 

Employer : Care Squad Pty Ltd 
Location: 214 Hampstead Rd, Clearview SA 5085 
Position: Full-time
Salary Range: $75,000 to $85,000 plus superannuation


ABOUT US

At Care Squad, we have a mission to improve the quality of life for people living with a disability, build confidence, dignity, and assistance to develop personal skills. As a small provider based in South Australia, we have a dedicated and caring team that focuses on the individual and their own personal wants, needs, and goals, rather than a faceless bureaucracy for whom you are simply a number. 

POSITION OVERVIEW

We are seeking a compassionate and dedicated Aged or Disabled Carer to join our dynamic team. In this role, you will provide personal care support to elderly clients, individuals with disabilities and ensuring their well-being by assisting with daily activities to enhance their quality of life. You will be responsible for providing personal care, emotional support, and assistance with household tasks. Your work will make a significant difference in the lives of those you support.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Personal Care Assistance: Provide compassionate support with daily personal care tasks such as bathing, dressing, grooming, and toileting, ensuring clients’ dignity and comfort.

Support with Mobility: Assist clients with mobility needs, including transferring, repositioning, and using mobility aids to ensure safety and independence.

Medication Assistance: Aid with medication reminders and ensure clients adhere to prescribed medication schedule, while observing and reporting any health changes.

Daily Living Activities: Support clients with household tasks like meal preparation, cleaning, laundry, and shopping, promoting a safe and comfortable living environment and accompanying aged and disabled persons during daily activities.

Companionship & Emotional Support: Offer companionship and encourage social engagement, ensuring clients feel valued, supported, and emotionally connected.

Care Plan Implementation: Collaborate with care management teams to follow and update personalized care plans, ensuring each client’s needs are met with respect and individualized attention.

Documentation & Reporting: Accurately record care provided and report any changes in clients’ health, behavior, or environment to supervisors to ensure ongoing quality of care.

Promote Independence: Empower clients to maintain as much independence as possible in their daily activities, fostering self-confidence and autonomy.

Continuous Learning: Participate in training programs and stay updated on best practices in personal care and disability support to provide the highest standard of care.

TO BE SUCCESSFUL IN THIS ROLE YOU WILL REQUIRE

•	AQF Certificate III in Individual support or higher relevant qualification is required.
•	12 months full-time or equivalent part-time or casual basis employment with proven experience is required in Aged / Disability Care Services. 
•	Valid Australian driver’s license is must, along with comprehensive car insurance. 
•	Applicants must be willing to accept shift allocations at client locations across metropolitan, regional, and outer regional South Australia, depending on operational requirements and client care needs. Flexibility to travel between client locations is an essential requirement of this position.
•	Strong interpersonal skills, a compassionate, patient approach.
•	Ability to work independently and as part of team.
•	A valid National Police Check, Working with Children Check and other NDIS entry level certificates are required.
•	First Aid, Manual Handling and CPR Certificate is required.

BENEFITS

•	Work in a supportive and inclusive team environment.
•	Opportunities for career development and training.
•	Flexible working arrangements to suit your lifestyle.
•	Meaningful work where you make a real impact.
•	Opportunity to make a real difference in the lives of others

OFFICE MANAGER (ANZSCO 512111)
Full-Time | Adelaide, South Australia
Salary: $75,000 – $95,000 + Superannuation

About Bide With Care Pty Ltd
Bide With Care Pty Ltd (BWC) is a registered NDIS provider committed to delivering high-quality disability and aged care support services across South Australia. We provide person-centred care tailored to participant goals, independence, dignity, and wellbeing.
Our services include disability support, community participation, in-home care, personal care, supported accommodation, and aged care services. Due to continued business growth and increasing operational demands, we are seeking an experienced and highly organised Office Manager to oversee our office administration, operational systems, compliance functions, and staff coordination.

About the Role
The Office Manager is responsible for organising and controlling the administrative functions and resources of the office, including office systems, administrative staff, operational workflows, compliance systems, and business support functions.
This role plays a critical leadership function in ensuring efficient daily operations, regulatory compliance, workforce coordination, and continuous business improvement.

Key Responsibilities
Office Operations & Service Planning
•	Oversee daily office operations and administration functions to ensure smooth and efficient service delivery.
•	Contribute to the planning and review of office services, priorities, and service standards.
•	Develop, implement, and improve administrative systems, workflows, and reporting structures.
•	Drive accountability, workflow visibility, and operational efficiencies.
Resource Allocation & Staff Coordination
•	Allocate human resources, office space, equipment, and operational resources effectively.
•	Assign work to administrative staff and monitor work performance.
•	Coordinate operational communication between support workers, coordinators, nurses, and management.
•	Support workforce planning, scheduling, and resource allocation.
Compliance & Records Management
•	Manage company records, participant documentation, and office filing systems.
•	Maintain service agreements, incident reports, risk assessments, compliance registers, and internal records.
•	Ensure documentation complies with NDIS Practice Standards and Quality & Safeguards requirements.
•	Support preparation for audits, regulatory reporting, and compliance reviews.
Financial & Accounts Administration
•	Assist with accounts payable and receivable functions.
•	Manage invoices, purchase orders, reconciliations, and payment processing.
•	Assist with payroll coordination and financial administration.
•	Support budgeting and expenditure monitoring.
Operational Liaison & Problem Resolution
•	Liaise with healthcare professionals, participants, families, and external stakeholders to coordinate business operations.
•	Facilitate prompt resolution of operational, compliance, and administrative issues.
•	Support management with business planning and operational improvement initiatives.
Human Resources Coordination
•	Coordinate onboarding, recruitment support, staff induction, and compliance documentation.
•	Maintain HR records, staff training registers, and performance documentation.
•	Assist with personnel activities including hiring, performance management, payroll coordination, and supervision.
WHS & Legislative Compliance
•	Ensure compliance with occupational health and safety regulations.
•	Maintain workplace safety records and risk management systems.
•	Ensure operations comply with relevant legislation, government regulations, and internal policies.

Essential Skills & Experience
•	Diploma, Advanced Diploma, Associate Degree or higher in Business Administration, Management, Office Administration, or related field.
OR
•	Minimum three years’ relevant experience in office management or business administration.
•	Strong leadership and organisational skills.
•	Demonstrated experience managing office systems and administration functions.
•	Experience managing records, compliance systems, and operational workflows.
•	Strong financial administration and reporting capability.
•	Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills.

Desirable
•	Experience in disability services, aged care, healthcare, or community services.
•	Knowledge of NDIS compliance and regulatory frameworks.
•	Experience in rostering and workforce coordination.

Why Join BWC?
•	Work with a growing and reputable NDIS provider.
•	Join a supportive and purpose-driven team.
•	Opportunity to contribute to meaningful outcomes for participants.
•	Leadership role with career growth opportunities.
If you are a highly motivated and experienced professional looking to contribute to operational excellence in a growing care organisation, we encourage you to apply.

Bowhill Engineering is seeking a motivated and detail-focused Project Assistant to join our team and support the delivery of major infrastructure projects through advanced digital
systems and production support. This is an exciting opportunity to work at the forefront of fabrication technology, helping drive a smarter, more connected and paperless workshop environment using industry-leading tools including FabStation and HoloLens AR. Specialising in large government infrastructure projects and complexity done excellently, Bowhill Engineering is powered by technology and driven by great people to optimise and build structures that matter.


About the Role
The Project Assistant plays a key role in strengthening quality, certainty and production flow by embedding advanced digital tools into everyday workshop and project execution. Working closely with Project, Production and Quality teams, you will support digital QA systems, production readiness, reporting and continuous improvement initiatives across the business. Through real-time data, visual verification and disciplined systems, you will help ensure fabrication is built right the first time while reducing rework and improving communication between teams. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys problem solving, technology, organisation and process improvement, while working in a fast-paced fabrication and manufacturing environment.


Key Responsibilities & Requirements
-Support and maintain digital QA systems including FabStation and HoloLens AR
-Assist with production readiness, work packs and planning coordination
-Ensure real-time production and QA data is accurate and up to date
-Support workshop teams with clear and accessible project information
-Monitor planned versus actual production performance and reporting
-Assist with compliance tracking, reporting and system updates
-Identify opportunities for improvement and help implement smarter processes
-Work collaboratively across Project, Production and Quality teams
-Help strengthen transparency, communication and workflow efficiency across projects
-Support continuous improvement initiatives and maintain OFI registers

Experience & Qualifications
-Current Driver’s Licence (Manual)
-Experience in steel fabrication, construction or manufacturing environments (desirable)
-Strong organisational and time management skills
-Excellent written and verbal communication skills
-Competent IT skills including MS Word, Excel & Outlook
-Experience with production software, Tekla or MS Project (desirable)
-Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings
-Strong attention to detail and problem-solving ability
-Understanding of WHS requirements and safe work practices

What We Offer
-Opportunity to work on major infrastructure projects of national significance
-Exposure to advanced digital fabrication and QA technology
-Career growth opportunities into a Production Systems Analyst role
-Supportive and collaborative team environment
-Employee Assistance Program (EAP)Employee Health Assistance
-Active Social Club and strong workplace culture
-Modern workplace with multiple workshops on site
-Enjoy the River Murray lifestyle
-Join an Employer of Choice in the Murraylands

About Us
Based in Bowhill, South Australia (90 mins from Adelaide, 40 mins from Murray Bridge, 30 mins from Mannum), Bowhill Engineering has built a national reputation for delivering large, complex steel structures with precision and pride — all from one location.
Apply Now - Bring your confidence in new technology & software, your analytical skills, quality focus & ability to capture, interpret & measure production data - we have an immediate spot waiting for you!
Submit your cover letter, resume, and three references via the Bowhill Engineering website.
For more information, contact HR Manager, Samantha Krollig on (08) 8570 4208.

COOK – FULL TIME

BUSINESS:  PAPADOPOULOS BROTHERS PTY LTD
ABN: 68 607 569 380
TRADING AS: Meli Annandale
LOCATION: 88 View Street, Annandale NSW 2038
SALARY: $79,500 – $83,000 + Superannuation (commensurate with experience)
EMPLOYMENT TYPE: Full-time (minimum 38 hours per week)

Job Published: 3 July 2026


ABOUT THE BUSINESS
Meli Annandale is a contemporary neighbourhood café located in Annandale, NSW, providing high-quality breakfast, brunch, and lunch dining within a modern hospitality environment. The café offers a diverse menu featuring freshly prepared contemporary Australian café cuisine, specialty coffee, and seasonal menu offerings, with a strong focus on quality ingredients, presentation, and customer experience.
The business operates a full-service dine-in model with prepared-to-order meals delivered across continuous daily service. Kitchen operations involve fresh ingredient preparation, coordinated food production, and efficient workflow management to meet varying customer demand, particularly during peak breakfast, brunch, and weekend trading periods.
The commercial kitchen operates under established systems and procedures, incorporating food preparation, cooking, plating, stock management, and strict compliance with Australian food safety, hygiene, and workplace health and safety standards to ensure consistent service quality and operational efficiency.

ABOUT THE ROLE
The position of Cook is a hands-on operational role responsible for preparing, cooking, and presenting menu items in accordance with established recipes, quality standards, and service requirements within a contemporary café environment. The role requires the ability to manage allocated kitchen sections, maintain consistency across breakfast, brunch, and lunch service, and contribute to the efficient day-to-day operation of a commercial kitchen.
The successful candidate will work collaboratively within a team-based environment, demonstrating initiative in food preparation, coordinating workflow during service, maintaining food quality and presentation standards, and ensuring compliance with food safety and hygiene requirements.
The primary place of employment will be Meli Annandale, 88 View Street, Annandale NSW 2038. From time to time, the successful candidate may also be required to perform duties at the employer's associated hospitality venue, Sabine Bondi, Shop 505/500 Oxford Street, Bondi Junction NSW 2022, to support operational requirements. Duties performed at either location will remain consistent with the position of Cook and will be undertaken under the direction of the employer.
The role also provides ongoing opportunities for professional development through structured on-the-job training and exposure to a range of contemporary café kitchen operations and cooking techniques.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

FOOD PREPARATION AND COOKING
•	Prepare, cook, and present a range of breakfast, brunch, and lunch menu items in accordance with established recipes, quality standards, and presentation requirements.
•	Undertake ingredient preparation, including washing, cutting, portioning, marinating, and pre-service mise en place to support efficient kitchen operations.
•	Apply appropriate cooking techniques including grilling, frying, roasting, baking, poaching, and sautéing while maintaining consistency in quality and presentation.
•	Follow standardised recipes and portion controls to ensure consistency, minimise wastage, and meet service expectations.
•	Adjust food preparation and cooking methods where required to accommodate service volumes, dietary requirements, and special customer requests.

SERVICE AND KITCHEN OPERATIONS
•	Support efficient kitchen workflow during breakfast, brunch, and lunch service to ensure timely preparation and delivery of meals.
•	Manage allocated kitchen sections, ensuring workstations are organised and service-ready prior to and during operational periods.
•	Communicate effectively with kitchen and front-of-house staff to support efficient service delivery and order accuracy.
•	Assist with menu execution, daily specials, and seasonal menu offerings in accordance with business requirements.
•	Adapt workflow during busy service periods while maintaining food quality, presentation, and operational efficiency.

STOCK CONTROL AND KITCHEN ORGANISATION
•	Assist in receiving, inspecting, and storing deliveries to ensure product quality and compliance with storage requirements.
•	Implement stock rotation practices, including FIFO, to maintain freshness and minimise wastage.
•	Monitor ingredient usage and report stock shortages or inconsistencies to senior kitchen staff.
•	Assist with stocktakes and maintain organised storage areas to support efficient kitchen operations.
•	Ensure appropriate labelling, storage, and handling of food products in accordance with food safety standards.

FOOD SAFETY AND COMPLIANCE
•	Maintain compliance with food safety legislation and safe food handling procedures.
•	Maintain high standards of hygiene and cleanliness across workstations, equipment, utensils, and food preparation areas.
•	Monitor storage, cooking, and holding temperatures to ensure compliance with food safety requirements.
•	Follow workplace food safety procedures, including HACCP-based practices where applicable.
•	Comply with Workplace Health and Safety requirements, including the safe operation of commercial kitchen equipment.

GENERAL DUTIES AND TEAM CONTRIBUTION
•	Maintain a clean, organised, and efficient workstation throughout each shift.
•	Follow instructions from senior kitchen staff and management with accuracy and attention to detail.
•	Work collaboratively within a team environment to support efficient kitchen operations during busy service periods.
•	Demonstrate reliability, professionalism, punctuality, and a positive approach to work.
•	Participate in ongoing training and professional development to enhance culinary skills and operational performance.

MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS
•	Relevant qualification in Commercial Cookery (Certificate III or higher) or a closely related field, or a minimum of one (1) year of relevant experience within a commercial kitchen environment.
•	Demonstrated experience preparing and cooking food within a commercial café, restaurant, or hospitality environment.
•	Sound knowledge of food safety standards, kitchen hygiene, and safe food handling practices.
•	Ability to work efficiently within a fast-paced commercial kitchen environment.
•	Availability to work weekends, public holidays, and varied rostered shifts as required.

KEY COMPETENCIES
•	Technical Cooking Proficiency
•	Contemporary Café Food Preparation
•	Recipe Interpretation & Food Presentation
•	Time Management
•	Kitchen Workflow & Operational Awareness
•	Attention to Detail
•	Communication & Team Collaboration
•	Problem Solving
•	Food Safety & Compliance
•	Commitment to Continuous Improvement

HOW TO APPLY
Please submit a one-page CV outlining your relevant experience, qualifications, and availability. Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted
